findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion (or expand the `[operator-attested]` Verified +1 criterion) that explicitly exercises the raised-cap path against a live boundary — e.g., 'attempt to run completion recovery against a synthetic or real context of ≥ 34,282 chars with the live model and confirm a verdict is returned rather than a context-bound refusal' — OR document a rationale for why the live boundary is excluded (e.g., the operator's Verified +1 vote constitutively includes a live close attempt on a ≥34K-char ticket).
evidence: 'Unit tier with an injected fake runner (no billable calls).'
AC1: 'asserted by a test parameterized on those two measured sizes' — the test uses a fake runner, not a live model
AC7: '[operator-attested] the change lands with LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1' — plan does not describe what live exercise Verified +1 entails
'This does not close 9fd4' — the actual blocked ticket is explicitly not closed by this plan, so no real ticket traverses the new path as evidence
findings.finding: The plan raises a live code path (completion-recovery now forwards contexts up to 100,000 chars to the model), but no acceptance criterion exercises that path against a live or semi-live model boundary. All proving commands use an injected fake runner that bypasses the actual model call. The operator-attested `Verified +1` AC is not described as an end-to-end exercise of the new cap, and E6(f) states that green offline tests plus a signed completion verdict are necessary but NOT sufficient when a cutover path has a live/external boundary.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — all ACs; Testing section ('Unit tier with an injected fake runner (no billable calls)')
scenarios: The unit tests pass on the new cap but a latent issue (e.g., model API refusal on a 100K-char prompt, a serialization truncation upstream of the model call, or a timeout) only manifests on a live call. The fake runner masks it, and the signed verdict is issued on mocked evidence.
findings.suggested_fix: Amend the operator-attested AC to read: '[operator-attested] the change lands with LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1, where Verified includes a live completion-recovery run against a context of ≥ 34,282 chars confirming a verdict is returned rather than a context-bound refusal.' This makes the live boundary explicit without requiring a new billable-by-default test.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Document (in the plan and in `docs/llm-framework.md`) that 100,000 chars ≈ 25,000 tokens and confirm this is within the minimum supported model window; if the system must support models with smaller windows, add a startup assertion or pre-call guard so the cap remains a controlled refusal rather than an opaque API error.
evidence: 'sizing.largest_window_tokens returns the same ceiling for every model including unknown ones, so the derivation would be both a unit error and insensitive to the configured model'
'A stated constant with a recorded rationale is honest; a fake derivation is not'
No statement anywhere in the plan that 100,000 chars ≈ 25,000 tokens is verified to be within the token window of every model the system may call
The plan's own cost reasoning ('recovery sends the whole context once per criterion') confirms each individual model call may carry up to 100,000 chars
findings.finding: The plan asserts that raising `_MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS` to 100,000 chars is safe to pass to the model, but never verifies that 100,000 chars fits within the actual token budget of the configured model(s). The plan explicitly rejects model-window derivation (correctly noting `sizing.largest_window_tokens` is inaccurate), yet that rejection leaves the new constant unanchored to any real model limit. The plan mentions 'unknown models' as a reason the derivation is broken — the same 'unknown models' argument means the new constant could exceed a configured model's window.
findings.location: Approach section — 'Alternative rejected — derive the cap from the model window' and `_MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS` = 100,000 constant
scenarios: A site configured to use a smaller or older model (e.g., a 16K-token context model) would receive a 100,000-char (~25K token) payload and fail at the API layer, producing an opaque error rather than the controlled refusal the old cap provided.
If a future 'unknown model' is configured with a smaller window, the constant silently becomes an over-limit value with no invariant test to catch it.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence to the 'Approach' rationale: '100,000 chars ≈ 25,000 tokens at the ~4 chars/token average, which is below the minimum context window of all models this system is certified to run against ([list them or cite a config key]); the invariant test added for the criteria-vs-context bound should also assert this.'. If the set of supported models is open-ended, add a pre-call guard in `completion_recovery.py` that checks the assembled context size against the model's reported window before issuing any API call.

findings.finding: The evidence sub-agent call in `_recover()` is submitted with `reviewers=['completion-verifier-evidence']`, but no reviewer with that ID exists anywhere in the catalog: it is absent from `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/index.json`, has no corresponding `.md` file in `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/`, and `get_prompt('completion-verifier-evidence')` would raise `PromptNotFound`. The plan's scope section lists `completion_recovery.py` as a touched file but does not mention defining or registering this reviewer. Because the `reviewers` field is stamped as `reviewer_id` in findings and used for tracing/telemetry, this dangling reference produces an undefined agent surface in every recovery evidence call: audit logs and Langfuse traces will reference a reviewer that has no specification, making post-hoc review of recovery runs unauditable.
scenarios: A post-incident review queries Langfuse/session logs for 'completion-verifier-evidence' runs to audit recovery decisions — the reviewer has no associated specification, so the audit surface is undefined.

A future caller that resolves reviewer metadata from the `reviewers` field (e.g. a tracing tool that fetches the prompt text for the labeled reviewer_id) will hit a PromptNotFound error for this label.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a `completion_verifier_evidence.md` file to `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/` with the same front-matter pattern as `completion_verifier_finalizer.md` (schema_version, title, category: completion-recovery, execution_mode: agentic, outputs: text) and a corresponding entry in `index.json`, mirroring how `completion-verifier-finalizer` is handled. Alternatively, change `reviewers=["completion-verifier-evidence"]` to `reviewers=["completion-verifier"]` as the nearest cataloged reviewer, since the sub-agent performs the same evidence-gathering role.
